A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGPO study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison, including material moved from v2's appendices into v5's main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original offline and online training results, judge-model ablations, repeated-run evaluations, and simulations of the stylized learning dynamics.

after.justification: v5 retains these original training experiments, ablations, repeated-run results, and simulations in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Equation (2) changes the sigmoid exponent from beta(RTS-gamma) to -beta(RTS-gamma), reversing the ordering of rewards for incorrect trajectories: longer correct prefixes now receive higher rewards. This materially changes the reward mapping as specified, although the surrounding SGPO procedure is retained. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LIMO and AIME1997-2023 training coverage and the same nine mathematical evaluation benchmarks, including Chinese tasks. The removed illustrative AIME question does not represent a distinct task or evaluation environment.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same untrained baselines, positive-only offline training comparison, and online GRPO comparator. VinePPO is newly discussed in v5 but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported models, decoding settings, group sizes, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. v5 explains pass@k and avg@k more explicitly; it does not introduce different metrics or testing procedures.

E4.justification: v5 removes Remark 3.2's concrete letter-pairing AIME failure example. Judge-strength, reward-scaling, voting, entropy, and learning-dynamics analyses are retained. The entropy and simulation analyses move into the main text, while new Figure 3 redisplays existing ablation results.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 4 retain the same repeated-run information and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. v5's Figure 3 visualizes these existing statistics without adding runs or a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1-5 and findings in the retained learning and entropy curves are unchanged. v5 removes the specific finding that DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and DeepSeek-V3-0324 both failed the illustrative AIME problem within 16 rollouts. It also adds a derived 2.5% overall training-overhead estimate, rather than a new timing measurement.

T1.justification: v5 adds derivations of the previously stated population gradients and likelihood updates. It corrects derivative denominators and the concavity function in Lemma C.1/B.1, removes erroneous one-half factors in the theorem's base case, and restores missing squares in its final induction step. These refine the existing theory; Theorem 3.3's conclusions and Table 6's coefficients remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace broad claims of consistent improvements with average-performance benefits that are not uniform across benchmarks and depend on negative-sample informativeness. The central SGPO contribution, simplified acceleration result, and distinction from knowledge distillation remain.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly acknowledges that identical judged rewards can still yield zero advantages and that noisy, short, or early-failing trajectories can reduce benefits or cause underperformance. It also clarifies the idealized theory's boundaries and explains the limitations of GRPO-centered benchmarking without PRM comparisons.

D1.justification: v5 adds implementation values stated as '10 and 0.5' for the previously symbolic reward-scaling parameters. It calculates approximately 2.5% end-to-end overhead from the already reported 10% judging overhead during three of twelve epochs. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: v5 adds five references, including VinePPO, GenEnv, and two Chen et al. 2026 papers. It positions VinePPO as complementary process-level credit assignment and explains the study's focus on outcome-based GRPO comparisons. The broader related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v5 substantially reorganizes the exposition: the stylized setup and full theorem proof move into Section 3.2, replacing the proof sketch, while former appendix experimental discussions enter the main text. It also expands background explanations, rewrites the abstract and conclusion, and adds a benchmarking-scope discussion.

P2.justification: v5 adds a prominent pipeline diagram and a combined visualization of existing means and standard deviations. It moves the appendix simulation and entropy plots into the main text, removes the redundant standalone simulation panel, and redistributes tables and captions. This is substantial visual reorganization without new benchmark tables.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects the reward formula and several proof expressions, supplies missing derivations, and qualifies broad performance claims to better reflect the mixed results in Table 2. These improve the existing study's internal consistency and clarity. Removing the concrete AIME example weakens one illustration, but the net effect is a limited improvement rather than new empirical validation.
